title: Trial Balance and Rectification of Errors

topics.title: Meaning and objectives of a trial balance

concepts.learning_objective: State the meaning of a trial balance and the purpose it serves in the accounting process.
Explain why a tallied trial balance checks arithmetical accuracy but is not conclusive proof of correct accounts.
Identify whether an account normally shows a debit or a credit balance in the trial balance.

topics.title: Methods of preparing a trial balance

concepts.learning_objective: Prepare a trial balance by showing the debit and credit totals of each ledger account.
Prepare a trial balance from ledger balances and explain why this method is most used.
Describe the four-column totals-cum-balances method and its limitations.

topics.title: Significance of agreement and classification of errors

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish errors of commission from errors of complete and partial omission.
Identify errors of principle arising from wrong capital-revenue classification.
Explain how compensating errors leave the trial balance in agreement.
List the steps an accountant takes to detect errors when the trial balance does not tally.
Use half of the difference to trace an amount posted to the wrong side.
Recognise that a difference divisible by 9 suggests a transposition of figures.

topics.title: Rectification of errors not affecting the trial balance

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why two-sided errors do not affect the trial balance and are corrected by a journal entry.
Pass the rectifying journal entry for errors of omission, commission and principle in two accounts.

topics.title: Suspense account and errors affecting the trial balance

concepts.learning_objective: Rectify one-sided errors such as wrong posting and wrong casting through a suspense account.
Explain when a suspense account is opened, on which side it appears and how it is closed.
State the account used when errors of one year are rectified in the next accounting year.
